title: The kb plugin, capture, freshness and PR comments
bridge: The kb skill is like a search box with citations. You ask, it returns the top pages with a path and a commit sha, and you quote them. Except: the model decides when to open the box, and the skill's description is what makes that decision happen.
intro: Pages are useless if nobody reads them at the right moment. This lesson ships the four things that bring the brain to people and agents. A kb CLI plus skill that searches and cites. A /kb-capture command that turns a thread or PR into a draft page. A weekly digest that nudges owners, and a comment on fcp PRs that touch described code.

picture.caption: One CLI, four moments: an agent asks, a person captures, a Monday nudge, and a PR comment.

sections.h: The kb CLI and the skill that uses it (G6-10)
p: The plugin lives in rnd-kb-tooling/plugin/. It has three parts: plugin.json (name kb), bin/kb (a launcher on the Bash PATH while the plugin is on), and skills/kb/SKILL.md. The launcher runs kb_tools/search.py, which is shipped inside the plugin and uses only the standard library.
Standard library only is a design choice. People, agents (through the harness's kb_search tool), BRAIN-QA and the bot all rank pages the same way, with no install step.

kb search keeps a mirror of rnd-kb (~/.cache/rnd-kb, or $KB_DIR in agent VMs). It runs git pull --ff-only when the mirror is over an hour old. It reads index.json and ranks pages with BM25 over title, headings and body. It boosts pages whose applies_to covers --path. It prints the top 5 as rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>  title  (effective confidence, reviewed).

BM25 is a classic text ranking formula. A page scores higher when it contains the query words often and those words are rare across pages. kb show prints a page with its sha. kb propose pushes a branch and opens a PR with gh; it is for people only.
sections.because: We write the skill as goals and steps, with the citation format spelled out. The citation is what lets a reviewer check every claim.

code.text:
---
name: kb
description: "Use when you need to know how part of Rhino's system works, why it was built that way, or what was decided. Searches the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb), answers with citations as path@sha, and proposes a fix when a page is wrong."
when_to_use: "Questions like 'how does a code run reach the on-prem client?', 'why does cloud CI run on push?', 'what did we decide about agent VMs?'. Also before planning a change in an area you don't know well."
argument-hint: "[question, or a file path to find pages about it]"
allowed-tools: Bash(kb search *) Bash(kb show *) Read
---
# kb: the R&D brain

The brain is a small set of owned pages about how our system works and why. It holds reasons and decisions the
code doesn't show, so search it even when you feel sure.

1. `kb search "<question>"`; add `--path <file>` when you are about to change that file. Read the top pages with
   `kb show <path>`.
2. Weigh each page by its confidence and reviewed date. `low` or overdue means a lead, not a fact: confirm it in
   the code before you rely on it.
3. Cite each claim as `rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>`, exactly as the search prints it.
4. If the brain has no answer, say so plainly and say where you looked. Don't fill the gap from memory.
5. If a page is wrong or missing something you just confirmed: people run `kb propose <path>` and the page owner
   reviews it; agents add it to the PR's "harness suggestions" section instead.

notes.text: name matches the folder: skills/kb.
description: the first line says when to use it. This is what makes the model open the skill.
when_to_use gives example questions, so the model recognises the shape of a brain question.
allowed-tools: only kb search, kb show and Read. The skill cannot write or push.
Search even when you feel sure: the brain holds reasons the code does not show.
Step 2: low or overdue is a lead, not a fact. Confirm it in the code before relying on it.
Step 3: cite each claim as rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>, exactly as search prints it.
Step 4: no answer means say so and say where you looked. Never fill the gap from memory.
Step 5: a wrong page is fixed by kb propose (people) or noted in the PR's harness suggestions (agents).

callout.text: Why a CLI and not an MCP server? A CLI runs the same way in a terminal, in the harness and in CI. It is also the language boundary: the TypeScript harness calls the Python kb search as a process.

sections.h: /kb-capture: a thread or a PR becomes a draft (G6-12)
p: Much of what we learn sits in Slack threads and PR discussions that scroll away. kb-capture is a second skill in the same plugin, with disable-model-invocation: true, so it runs only when a person types /kb-capture. The input is a PR URL or a pasted thread.

The skill applies the data rules from DATA-SCOPE.md. A private-channel thread becomes a summary in our own words, with no quotes. Customer names and anything that looks like PHI are dropped. Keys, tokens and passwords are never copied.
sections.because: We make the skill user-only because a capture writes a page and opens a PR. Only a person should decide that a thread is worth a page.

code.text:
---
name: kb-capture
description: "Use when someone wants to save what was learned in a Slack thread or a PR as a brain page: drafts a page at confidence: low and opens a PR to RhinoHealth/rnd-kb for its owner."
argument-hint: "<PR URL or Slack permalink, or paste the thread after the command>"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(gh pr view *) Bash(kb lint *) Bash(kb propose *) Read Write
---
# kb-capture

Turn one discussion into one short page that a newcomer could act on.

1. Read the source. A PR: `gh pr view $ARGUMENTS --comments`. A Slack thread: the pasted text.
2. Follow DATA-SCOPE.md. From a private channel (#engineering, #eng-tooling, #devops, #claude-users) write a
   summary in your own words and quote nothing. Leave out customer names, personal details and anything that looks
   like patient data. Never copy a key, token or password.
3. Write the page from templates/page.md: what we learned, why, what to do next time, where to look. One screen.
4. Frontmatter: owner from OWNERS.yml (ask the user if unsure), reviewed today, confidence low, the PR URL or thread
   permalink in sources, applies_to when it is about code.
5. Run `kb lint`, then `kb propose <path>`, and share the PR link. The owner raises the confidence after checking.

notes.text: The description still says when to use it, for the person reading /help.
disable-model-invocation: true: the model never starts this skill on its own.
allowed-tools: gh pr view, kb lint, kb propose, Read, Write. Enough to draft and propose, nothing more.
Step 1: a PR is read with gh pr view $ARGUMENTS --comments; a thread is the pasted text.
Step 2: DATA-SCOPE.md inside the skill: private channels as summaries, no customer names, no secrets.
Step 3: the page follows templates/page.md: what we learned, why, what to do next time, where to look.
Step 4: frontmatter: owner from OWNERS.yml, reviewed today, confidence low, the URL as source.
Step 5: kb lint, kb propose, share the PR link. The owner raises confidence after checking.

p: Pages go stale quietly. kb freshness groups overdue pages by owner and posts one short Slack message per owner. It runs every Monday at 06:17 UTC from a workflow in rnd-kb.
OWNERS.yml gives each owner's Slack user or channel ID. The Slack app "Rhino Brain" is created now with only chat:write. The bot tickets in g6-6 add Socket Mode and read scopes to the same app.
No page is edited by the digest. Pages more than 2x overdue already read as low through effective_confidence() from g6-1.
sections.because: We group by owner and send one message each. One message with three links gets read; three separate pings get muted.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/src/kb_tools/freshness.py: weekly digest of overdue pages, one message per owner
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date

from slack_sdk import WebClient

from kb_tools.kb import load_owners, load_pages  # pages parsed with schema.Page

PAGE_URL = "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb/blob/main/{path}"


def digest(kb_dir: str, today: date) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    by_owner: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for path, page in load_pages(kb_dir):
        if page.due() >= today:
            continue
        late = (today - page.due()).days
        note = " (now read as low)" if page.effective_confidence(today) != page.confidence else ""
        by_owner[page.owner].append(f"• <{PAGE_URL.format(path=path)}|{page.title}>: {late} days overdue{note}")
    return by_owner

notes.text: defaultdict(list) makes by_owner[owner].append(...) work without checking the key first.
slack_sdk's WebClient: the plain Slack Web API client, enough for chat_postMessage.
load_owners and load_pages come from a small kb.py; pages are parsed with schema.Page.
The page URL template: GitHub's blob view of the page on main.
digest() returns owner to list of lines. It is pure, so a test can call it with a fixed today.
Skip pages that are not due yet. page.due() comes from the schema.
late: how many days overdue, for the message.
If effective_confidence differs from the page's own value, the page is already reading as low; say so.
A Slack line: bullet, link with the title, days overdue, the note.

p: post() does the Slack side. The first two weeks run with --dry-run, which prints the messages instead of sending them. So Shai can check the wording with two owners.
sections.because: We keep a --dry-run path because the first message an owner sees sets the tone for every later one.

notes.text: post() takes the KB folder, the Slack token (from the workflow secret) and the dry_run flag.
OWNERS.yml maps each owner to a Slack user or channel ID.
One loop per owner with overdue pages; date.today() is the real date here.
The ask is short and says what to do: read, fix, update reviewed.
Dry run: print and continue. Nothing reaches Slack.
The real send: chat_postMessage to the owner's Slack ID.

callout.text: The cron is 17 6 * * 1: Monday, 06:17 UTC. We use an odd minute on purpose, because many jobs fire on the hour and GitHub delays them.

sections.h: A comment on fcp PRs that touch described code (G6-16)
p: Code changes are the main reason pages go stale. The cheapest moment to fix a page is while the author still has the context. So a small workflow in fcp matches the PR's changed files against the applies_to globs in index.json. It posts one comment listing the pages and owners to check.
It is information only: never a required check, and it posts nothing when no page matches. One comment per PR, edited in place on each push. Agent PRs get it too; Nova reads it as a hint.
sections.because: We mint a scoped App token because this job reads rnd-kb and writes a comment on fcp. The job's own GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read another repo.

code.text:
# fcp/.github/workflows/kb-pages.yml: tells the author which brain pages describe the code they changed
name: kb-pages
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  pages:
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - id: app
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_ID }}

notes.text: Runs on opened, synchronize (a push) and ready_for_review.
The job's own token stays read-only; the App token does the comment.
fcp-runner-set: fcp's self-hosted ARC runners.
Pin by SHA. fetch-depth: 0 so git diff against the base sha works.
setup-uv, because kb touched runs with uvx below.
The rhino-kb App token: contents:read on rnd-kb and rnd-kb-tooling, pull-requests:write on fcp.
repositories narrows the token to the three repos.

p: The last step is four commands. List the changed files, fetch index.json from rnd-kb, run kb touched, and comment only if the output is not empty. kb touched is a new subcommand in rnd-kb-tooling: it prints a short markdown list (page, owner, which file matched), or nothing. You will write its core in the lab.
sections.because: We fetch index.json through the GitHub API instead of cloning rnd-kb. The job needs one file, and a clone would take longer than the match.

code.text:
private-key: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: RhinoHealth
          repositories: rnd-kb,rnd-kb-tooling,fcp
      - name: Find pages for the changed files and comment
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          git diff --name-only "$BASE"...HEAD > changed.txt
          gh api repos/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb/contents/index.json --jq .content | base64 -d > index.json
          uvx --from "git+https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb-tooling" \
            kb touched --index index.json --files changed.txt > comment.md
          if [ -s comment.md ]; then
            gh pr comment "$PR" --body-file comment.md --edit-last --create-if-none
          fi

notes.text: GH_TOKEN is the App token, so gh api and gh pr comment act as the rhino-kb App.
BASE: the PR's base commit, for the diff.
git diff --name-only base...HEAD: the files this PR changes, one per line.
gh api fetches index.json as base64 (the contents API) and decodes it.
uvx --from git+... runs kb touched from rnd-kb-tooling without cloning it by hand; the token is in the URL for the private repo.
-s: only if comment.md is not empty.
--edit-last --create-if-none: one comment per PR, updated on every push.

sections.ifInstead: If instead gh pr comment fails with 'Resource not accessible by integration', the App token lacks pull-requests:write on fcp. Ask DevOps to add it in the App's permissions (G6-04 planned it for this ticket).

Two changed files, like git diff --name-only would print.

These brain pages describe code this PR changes. Check them, or ask the owner:

lab.faded: fnmatch treats * like a shell: it matches across slashes, so fcp:.github/workflows/* also matches .github/workflows/sub/x.yml. Decide whether that is what you want, then change the match to use pathlib.PurePath(file).match(pattern) or glob semantics and rerun both cases. Say in a comment which you chose and why.
lab.alone: Write freshness_digest.py with the digest() function from the G6-14 block, reading pages with the schema from your g6-1 lab (PYTHONPATH=~/labs/kb/src). Give it two pages: one overdue by 10 days, and one 200 days overdue with review_every 90d. Print the two lines for their owner with a fixed today. The second line must carry '(now read as low)'.
lab.done: touched.py prints one line per matched page and nothing when nothing matches. Your digest prints the '(now read as low)' note only for the page that is more than twice overdue.

quiz.q: Why is kb search written with the standard library only?

options.text: Because pip is not allowed on agent VMs.
options.why: The VM has Python and uv; the reason is sameness, not a ban.

options.text: So people, the harness, BRAIN-QA and the bot rank pages the same way with no install step.
options.why: That is the stated reason in G6-10 and in ts_platform.md's 'what stays Python'.
BM25 is simple enough to write by hand, but that is a consequence, not the reason.

quiz.q: The kb-pages comment on an fcp PR is red. What should the author do?

options.text: Nothing is red: it is information only and never a required check.
options.why: G6-16: never a required check, no comment when nothing matches.

options.text: Update the listed pages before the PR can merge.
options.why: The comment asks the author to check the pages; it blocks nothing.

options.text: Ask the page owner to approve the PR.
options.why: Page owners review pages, not fcp PRs. Exactly one approval, from the usual reviewer.

quiz.q: When does the digest edit a page that is more than twice overdue?

options.text: It sets confidence: low in the file and commits.
options.why: No page edits; effective_confidence() computes low at read time.

options.text: Never; search, the index and the bot compute low from the dates.
options.why: G6-14: no page edits; the schema's effective_confidence does it everywhere.

options.text: It opens a PR that the owner must merge.
options.why: The digest only posts a Slack message per owner.

words.plain: The CLI command that pulls the rnd-kb mirror, ranks pages with BM25 and prints the top 5 as path@sha.
A text ranking formula: a page scores higher when it contains the query words often and those words are rare across pages.
A reference like rnd-kb/engineering/x.md@a1b2c3d: the page and the exact commit, so a reviewer can check the claim.
A SKILL.md field; true means only a person can start the skill by typing /its-name.
The command that matches changed files against applies_to globs in index.json and prints the pages to check.
Running a command so it prints what it would do without doing it; the digest's first two weeks.

remember: The brain reaches people through one small CLI. Search with citations for agents, capture for people and a Monday nudge for owners. And a PR comment while the context is still warm.
